target_refs.quote: the Madras-Bangalore Transport Company (West) continued to be in occupation of the premises even after the Caravan Goods Carrier Private Limited came in. They never effaced themselves.
We do not think that there was any sub-letting, assignment or parting with possession of the premises

element_targets.reason: The target court expressly found continued occupation by West and expressly rejected subletting, assignment, or parting with possession; this is nonfulfilment of the transfer/possession element, not merely a failure of proof.

The target court did not separately decide the statutory date predicate. The 1968 formation of Caravan and the 1979 petition chronology do not establish the date of a qualifying transfer, especially because the court found no such transfer.

The target court did not expressly adopt a finding that written landlord consent was absent. The frozen input contains only the landlord's allegation, and the target disposed of the section 14(1)(b) ground on the no-transfer determination.

target_refs.quote: We do not think that there was any sub-letting, assignment or parting with possession of the premises by Madras-Bangalore Transport Company (West) to Caravan Goods Carrier Private Limited so as to attract Section 14(1)(b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act.

issue_target.reason: The fixed section 14(1)(b) eviction ground is not supported at the target stage because the target court expressly rejected the necessary transfer/parting-with-possession element. The unresolved temporal and written-consent predicates are not inferred from the overall disposition.

gaps.description: The supplied section 14(1)(b) text is a current statutory reproduction whose historical consolidation for the target date is expressly unverified, so the proposal cannot certify that the reproduced wording is the authenticated historical text.

LAW:V09:CEL_CONTROL is a 2009 Supreme Court synthesis under a Goa rent statute and postdates the 1986 target decision. Its control/retention principle is therefore not used as a governing target-era Delhi condition without additional scope validation.

No frozen inventory fact establishes the date of any qualifying transfer. Fact f3 dates Caravan's formation to 1968 but expressly leaves unknown whether formation itself transferred any tenancy or possessory right.
The frozen input supplies only f5 as the landlord's no-consent allegation, and the target reasoning does not separately adopt absence of written consent.
